title: St John Ambulance: do not sweep a choking child's mouth
summary: The child page uses back blows and abdominal thrusts, and it says a finger sweep can push the object further down.
body: St John Ambulance's child choking page follows the adult order: ask, encourage a cough, five back blows, five abdominal thrusts, then 999 or 112 and repeat. It adds an explicit warning that was not the emphasis of the adult page: after each back blow, check the mouth and pick out an obvious obstruction, and do not sweep the mouth, because that could push the object further down the throat. Check the mouth again after every thrust. If the child becomes unresponsive, assess them for CPR.
